questions.q: What is the relationship between `docker run`, `docker create`, and `docker start`?
options: docker run only works after docker create has failed
They are unrelated commands with no overlap
docker create and docker start both start a running container immediately
docker run is shorthand for docker create (configure the container) followed by docker start (launch its main process)
questions.explain: docker create configures the container -- filesystem, config, network -- without running anything. docker start launches its main process. docker run performs both steps at once.

questions.q: What is the key difference between `docker stop` and `docker kill`?
options: docker stop sends SIGTERM and gives the process a grace period before forcing it with SIGKILL; docker kill sends SIGKILL immediately with no grace period
docker kill only works on paused containers
There is no difference; they are aliases for the same operation
docker stop deletes the container, while docker kill only stops it
questions.explain: docker stop allows a clean shutdown by sending SIGTERM and waiting (typically 10 seconds) before forcing SIGKILL. docker kill skips the grace period entirely.

questions.q: What does `docker pause` actually do to a container?
options: It reduces the container's CPU allocation to zero but keeps it writable
It permanently disables the container until it's removed and recreated
It freezes every process inside the container using the host's cgroup freezer -- nothing runs, but nothing exits
It stops the container and deletes its filesystem changes
questions.explain: docker pause uses the cgroup freezer to suspend all processes in the container in place, useful for inspecting state mid-incident without anything changing further.

questions.q: Why would Northbridge's checkout service use `docker stop` instead of `docker kill` during a routine deploy?
options: docker stop is faster than docker kill in every case
docker kill doesn't exist for containers running web applications
There is no meaningful difference for a checkout service
docker stop gives the running process a chance to finish in-flight requests before shutting down, which docker kill does not allow
questions.explain: docker stop's grace period lets the application shut down cleanly -- finishing requests already in progress -- whereas docker kill terminates immediately with no warning.
